author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can view which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page listing every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name; specialty-driven, single page, no pagination.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory lists every specialty by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name in first-name-then-last-name order
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarians under it
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear anywhere on the page
All specialties render on one page with no pagination
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
notes: Inverse view of REQ-VET-001. The page is driven by the specialty table, so a specialty held by no vet appears with an empty vet list; conversely, a vet with no specialty is absent (the page lists specialties, not the vet roster). This asymmetry is deliberate and differs from REQ-VET-001, where a vet with no specialty is shown as holding none.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Inverse view of REQ-VET-001, sitting in the existing vet feature package. No new pattern or module: it composes three in-force patterns from architecture-principles.md — Repository (one per aggregate root), Web controller (server-rendered), and Thymeleaf page — exactly as VetController/VetRepository/vetList.html already do. The one design decision the PRD left open is how the specialty side is read. Because the page is specialty-driven and must list a specialty held by no vet, the read must originate from the specialties table; the vet_specialties join is mapped only from the Vet side and cannot surface an unheld specialty. Decision: a NEW SpecialtyRepository (mirroring PetTypeRepository's explicit name-ordered @Query), plus reuse of the existing VetRepository.findAll(); the controller inverts vet->specialty into specialty->vets for presentation. Do NOT add an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) to Specialty and do NOT add a specialty query to VetRepository (that breaks one-repository-per-aggregate-root). Verdict minor: established patterns, thin controller-side inversion layer, one overridden file target. No ADR (straightforward implementation choice, obvious rationale). No system-design.md write now — its Contracts table is derived-from-code; doc-sync adds the SpecialtyController/SpecialtyRepository rows and the REQ-SPEC-001 mapping after the code lands. Oracle N/A (IDE MCP not connected); covering code confirmed by Read of VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, PetTypeRepository.java, BaseEntity.java and grep of messages.properties.
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html on SpecialtyController, binding no request parameters (no pagination), returning view vets/specialtyList — matches the /vets.html convention
SpecialtyController depends on SpecialtyRepository (new) and VetRepository (existing, reused); constructor injection, no service layer, consistent with VetController

Controller assembles the specialty->vets grouping as a view model: seed an ordered structure from every specialty (name order), then file each vet under each specialty it holds; vets with no specialty are never filed (AC3), specialties with no vet keep an empty list (AC2)
Template reuses existing message keys specialties/name/none; no new bundle key, so the REQ-LANG-002 build-time key-parity test is untouched

patterns.description: Repository for a lookup aggregate root with an explicit name-ordered @Query — the precedent SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() mirrors; puts stable specialty ordering at the DB layer (AC edge-case 1)
Web controller assembling a view model in a private helper before returning the view name — the precedent for the controller-side inversion; no business rule, presentation grouping only
th:each over the collection with th:text full-name rendering (firstName + ' ' + lastName) — reuse for the vet rows under each specialty; Thymeleaf auto-escaping covers XSS on stored names

risks.risk: BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so Specialty instances compare by object identity. The specialties from SpecialtyRepository and the specialties inside Vet.getSpecialties() are distinct object instances (separate reads/transactions); keying a Map<Specialty,...> by the entity object silently drops every vet, so held specialties render empty.
risks.mitigation: Key the grouping by Specialty.getId() (stable, DB-assigned), not by the Specialty object. A controller test with a vet holding a seeded specialty catches a regression here (test specialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians).

risks.risk: An inverse lazy @ManyToMany(mappedBy) on Specialty would introduce N+1 across specialties and, with spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled, risk LazyInitializationException during render.
risks.mitigation: Do not add the inverse mapping. Read specialties and vets in two queries; Vet.specialties is FetchType.EAGER so VetRepository.findAll() returns fully-initialized specialty sets, and the inversion runs on materialized objects outside any open session.

risks.risk: Deterministic ordering of vets under each specialty (AC edge-case 1) is a controller concern; the vet_specialties fetch order is arbitrary.
risks.mitigation: Sort each specialty's vet list by a stable key (last name then first name, or first then last to match the displayed 'firstName lastName'); pick one and assert it in the stable-order test.

notes: File-target override: the prd-entry listed VetRepository.java, implying a specialty query on the vet repository; superseded here by a new SpecialtyRepository.java to honor one-repository-per-aggregate-root, with VetRepository reused unchanged (findAll). URL bound to exactly GET /specialties.html per the product-owner constraint, matching /vets.html; read-only, NG-2 unchanged, no write path and no new trust boundary (same open-route posture as every route, NG-1). REQ-SYS-001 requires nav to owner and vet areas only, so a menu link to the specialty page is out of scope; the route is reachable directly. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the handoff log, nothing to audit.
